1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 a6 5.N.name: Sicilian Defence: Kan Variation, Wing Attack

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 a6 5.N.strategy: Supports e4 and eyes the b5-pawn, so the long-diagonal pressure Black planned meets a solid defence. White develops naturally and keeps the centre intact while Black's queenside advance has loosened Black's own camp.

Meets the pressure on e4 with a fianchetto: the bishop on g2 guards the pawn and contests the diagonal. It is a sound but slower and less natural way to defend than the bishop on d3, and does nothing against Black's queenside advance.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 a6 5.N.name: Sicilian Defence: Kan Variation, Wing Attack, Fianchetto Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 a6 5.N.strategy: Attacks the d4 knight, which nothing defends because Bd3 blocks the queen's guard, so White has to spend a tempo on it. Black keeps the queenside storm in reserve (...b4 to chase the c3 knight, ...Bb7 against e4) and gains time for it.

Puts the bishop on the long diagonal against e4, which only the c3 knight guards: the point of the whole ...b5 advance. With ...b4 ready to chase that knight, White has to shore up e4 with the fianchettoed bishop and accept a slower, more strategic fight.
